title: Inquest called into RCMP custody death
article: The office of Manitoba's chief medical examiner is reviewing the March 2007 death of a Winnipeg man who met his demise while in the custody of Selkirk RCMP.

Provincial Chief Medical Examiner, Dr. A. Thambirajah Balachandra, has called an inquest into the death of Randy George Krasnesky, 35, who was pronounced dead at the Selkirk & District General Hospital on the evening of March 16, 2007, the accidental victim of an acute cocaine overdose.

The Selkirk Journal reported, on the night in question RCMP pulled over a vehicle near the corner of Main Street and Schultz Avenue in the City of Selkirk around 7 p.m. for a suspected violation of the Controlled Drugs and Substances Act.
A male passenger was handcuffed and placed into the police cruiser without incident. He soon took sick, vomited, began convulsing and became unresponsive.
Mounties removed him from the car and placed him in the recovery position as they waited for paramedics. He was transported by ambulance to hospital, and died just before 9 p.m.
The diver of the vehicle - an adult female - was not charged and was not involved in the investigation.

An autopsy and toxicology screen were completed but an RCMP spokesman at the time said there was no "overt cause of death." Police remained tight-lipped about Krasnesky's demise for several months and would not reveal test results despite repeated calls from the Journal.

The medical examiner's official report revealed the autopsy discovered a torn condom with a knot in the end in Krasnesky's stomach. It is believed the condom contained cocaine and resulted in the overdose.

The provincial inquiry was called in accordance with The Fatalities Inquiries Act to fulfill the requirement of a mandatory inquest as defined by legislation and to determine the circumstances relating the Krasnesky's death.
The inquest is also hoping to determine what, if anything, can be done to prevent similar deaths in the future.
The date, time and location of the inquest will be determined at a later date.
